statement: Under the CCDR's BAU dry-hot scenario, drought risk rises fivefold by mid-century and climate change lowers annual GDP about 6 percent by 2050, affecting agriculture, hydropower and labor productivity.
compact_statement: Under the CCDR's BAU dry-hot scenario, drought risk rises fivefold by mid-century and climate change lowers annual GDP about 6 percent by 2050, affecting agriculture, hydropower and labor productivity.
uncertainty: Scenario-specific model result, not a single expected outcome.

statement: CCDR says shock-responsive social protection backed by disaster risk financing has cushioned recent drought impacts; it recommends scaling early warning and adaptive social protection.
compact_statement: CCDR says shock-responsive social protection backed by disaster risk financing has cushioned recent drought impacts; it recommends scaling early warning and adaptive social protection.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 7, Key Report Messages on social protection and disaster risk financing

uncertainty: Summary does not identify program coverage or isolate causal contribution.

statement: NAP says drought can reduce water quantity and quality; many rural communities rely on a single river or stream, and resulting scarcity affects users across provinces.
compact_statement: NAP says drought can reduce water quantity and quality; many rural communities rely on a single river or stream, and resulting scarcity affects users across provinces.
affected_groups: rural communities dependent on single water sources

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 30 (printed p. 23), social vulnerability matrix on drought and water sources

uncertainty: Qualitative risk matrix; no service-loss or population count.

statement: NAP rates drought-related groundwater exposure high and says low-rainfall areas have lower adaptive capacity because droughts occur frequently, including Southern and Eastern provinces in agro-ecological region I.
compact_statement: NAP rates drought-related groundwater exposure high and says low-rainfall areas have lower adaptive capacity because droughts occur frequently, including Southern and Eastern provinces in agro-ecological region I.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 31 (printed p. 24), groundwater and adaptive-capacity matrix

uncertainty: Qualitative area rating; no local trend series is given in this matrix.

statement: NAP links drought yield losses to lower smallholder income from crop, livestock and fish sales, with little adaptation finance in Southern, Western and Eastern provinces.
compact_statement: NAP links drought yield losses to lower smallholder income from crop, livestock and fish sales, with little adaptation finance in Southern, Western and Eastern provinces.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 34, financial vulnerability matrix for small-scale farmers

uncertainty: Assessment is qualitative and reports no income amount.

statement: NAP states higher temperatures and drought contribute to more frequent forest-fire risk in Southern, Western, Eastern and Central provinces.
compact_statement: NAP states higher temperatures and drought contribute to more frequent forest-fire risk in Southern, Western, Eastern and Central provinces.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 30, forestry vulnerability matrix on drought and fire risk

uncertainty: NAP presents a qualitative risk assessment, not province-level fire incidence counts.
